title: Seven Earths
sub: Seven rocky worlds, one tiny star
blurb: TRAPPIST-1 hosts seven roughly Earth-sized planets orbiting a single ultracool red dwarf — the largest known family of rocky worlds around one star.

title: A Star Like Jupiter
sub: Barely bigger than a gas giant
blurb: TRAPPIST-1 is just 12% the Sun's width and about 9% its mass — only a little larger than Jupiter. It is so cool it shines mostly in infrared light.

title: Smaller Than One Orbit
blurb: Every TRAPPIST-1 planet orbits closer to its star than Mercury does to the Sun. The whole seven-world system would fit comfortably inside Mercury's orbit.

title: A Year in Days
blurb: Because the planets hug their tiny star, their years are astonishingly short — from 1.5 days on the innermost world to about 19 days on the outermost.

title: The Water Zone
blurb: Planets e, f and g orbit within the habitable zone, where temperatures could let liquid water pool on a rocky surface.

title: Permanent Day & Night
blurb: The planets are likely tidally locked, keeping one face in eternal daylight and the other in endless night — with a ring of perpetual twilight in between.

title: Worlds That Fill the Sky
blurb: The planets are packed so closely that, from the surface of one, its neighbours can appear several times larger than our Moon looks from Earth.

title: 39 Light-Years Away
blurb: TRAPPIST-1 lies about 39 light-years away in Aquarius — near enough that telescopes can already probe its planets' atmospheres for signs of life.
